title: A sharp isoperimetric inequality for the Neumann--Poincaré operator in every dimension
summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, be a bounded connected domain with boundary of class $C^{1,α}$, where $0<α<1$. For the adjoint Neumann--Poincaré operator $K^*_{\partialΩ}$, normalised so that its distinguished eigenvalue is $1/2$, let $λ_j^+(Ω)$ denote the upper min--max values on the mean-zero energy space. We prove $\sum_{j=1}^{d}λ_j^+(Ω)\ge \frac{d-2}{2}.$ It follows that $λ_1^+(Ω)\ge \frac{d-2}{2d},$ with equality if and only if $Ω$ is a ball.
